trust_decision.summary: Remote XML fetched by readers (a sitemap, a Stripe sitemap partition, PubMed eutils responses) is parsed with stdlib xml.etree, which accepts inline DTD entity declarations; nothing decides that entity-bearing remote XML is untrusted before parsing.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names 'its sitemap parser'; SitemapReader._parse_sitemap is the class literally called sitemap reader and calls ET.fromstring on the fetched sitemap.

fix_sites.module_kind: separate integration package llama-index-readers-stripe-docs (copy of sitemap logic)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about 'the sitemap parser'; PubMed eutils responses come from a fixed NCBI government endpoint, not a user-supplied URL, so a solver can argue the PubMed reader is out of scope and trusted.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Namespaced sitemap parsing (findall/find with the sitemaps.org namespace) and filter-by-substring must keep returning <loc> URLs, including for sitemaps with an XML declaration or a DOCTYPE without entities; a fix that regex-strips input, rejects any '<!' or forbids all DTDs breaks legitimate documents.
